newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AGL says non-gas contribution grows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AGL says non-gas contribution grows.

text.p: The Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) said on Thursday almost 40 percent of its record annual net profit was derived from non-gas businesses.
"AGL is now a broadly based energy company with growing international businesses," chairman Richard Mason said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported a 32.2 percent jump in net profit to A$124.3 million for the 12 months to June 30.
AGl will pay a fully franked final dividend of 17 cents a share, up from 14 cents last year.
AGL said its 50 percent stake in Victorian electricity distributor Solaris Power contributed A$7.7 million to the company's earnings.
AGL Gas Companies natural gas volumes grew marginally over the previous year and tariff markets sales rose by almost six percent.
Contract sales volumes fell by two percent, largely reflecting the downturn in the building industry.
The company said five natural gas co-generation projects were completed during the year with a further seven now committed for 1996/97.
AGL Pipelines contribution to profit before interest and tax grew 15.1 percent to A$45.7 million, which included A$18.5 million from its 33.3 percent investment in Natural Gas Corp.

Property activities contributed A$13.5 million, while AGL's interests in Elgas, Industrial Pipe Systems and HC Extractions made a contribution of A$10.8 million. "Our entry into electricity distribution and retailing together with natural gas utilities, pipelines and LPG businesses has transformed AGL from a gas company to an energy company," Mason said. "This is in line with the company's broader strategy to compete effectively in the broader energy market." -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
